chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from someone he mentioned, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Karram, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If people were just two men, one of them would be the Imam.' And he said: 'The last one to die is the Imam, so that no one may have a claim against Allah that He left him without an authority from Him.'

key_terms.إمام: Imam (the divinely appointed leader and proof of God)
key_terms.حجة: Hujjah (proof, authority, or evidence from God)
key_terms.يَحُجَّ: Yahajja (to have a claim or argument against someone)

ai.seo_question: Why is the presence of the Imam necessary according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq underscores the theological necessity of the Imam's continuous presence as Allah's definitive proof (hujjah) upon humanity, ensuring divine justice is never compromised by a lack of guidance. It highlights the eschatological significance of the Imam's death as the terminal point of accountability, a concept central to Shia Usuli thought regarding the validity of religious obligation in the Imam's absence. The statement 'if people were only two, one would be the Imam' illustrates the Imam's indispensable role even in minimal communities, reinforcing his status as the axis of divine authority.
